takeaways.label: 31% YoY growth, volume-led and broad-based
takeaways.text: Three pillars (organic, new components, new customers) each contributed ~10%, putting the company on track for its 25% FY27 target.

takeaways.label: Wind is a share-gain story, not a demand story
takeaways.text: Despite flat Indian wind installations in H1, Gala grew by expanding wallet share from a 5%–30% base and beginning offshore wind exports.

takeaways.label: Chennai Phase 2 is the near-term capacity unlock
takeaways.text: Phase 1 is nearly full; Phase 2 comes online by January (possibly December), and management expects to start using it within 15 days to 1 month of commissioning, subject to order flow.

takeaways.label: Margin improvement is underway but gradual
takeaways.text: H1 EBITDA margin improved 1.3% net, helped by the absence of last year's forex loss; management targets 17%–19% and expects further improvement in coming quarters.

watch.label: What to watch next quarter
watch.text: The pace of Chennai Phase 2 ramp-up, progress on the European auto pilot lots, and whether the 10% inventory reduction target materializes.

points.label: Three equal growth pillars
points.text: Organic growth from existing products, new components sold to existing customers, and new customer additions each delivered roughly 10% of the ~30% revenue increase.

points.label: Q2 revenue included a catch-up
points.text: Approximately ₹3 crores of revenue held back from Q1 dispatches landed in Q2, modestly inflating the quarter's reported growth.

points.label: Wind growth decoupled from end-market
points.text: Indian wind installations were flat at 3.1 GW in H1, yet Gala grew by capturing share from its 5%–25%-30% wallet position with most wind OEMs and by adding the bolt product category after Chennai plant approvals.

points.label: Three industries driving the pipeline
points.text: Renewable energy (wind, electrolyzers), industrial (electrical equipment, off-highway equipment), and mobility (automotive growing ~15% in India, plus railways with new opportunities in gallock, disc spring, coil spring, and fasteners).

points.label: Export mix is shifting upward
points.text: Export sales share moved from 33% to 38% of total sales, adding nearly ₹5 crores, which also extended the working capital cycle to 90–100 days due to transit time and the number of days.

points.label: New application wins are stacking up
points.text: Customer approvals secured for critical applications in railway safety, offshore wind, and mining equipment; first bulk commercial electrolyzer order dispatched; European auto client at pilot lot stage with multiple lots due in Q3 and Q4.

quotes.text: Satish Kotwani: "These 3 pillars contribute approximately 10% each, which has resulted in approximately 30% growth. So I think how to see this growth, I think we are on the track to grow 25% this year."

points.label: Phase 1 is effectively full
points.text: Running at almost full Phase 1 capacity of ₹60 crores per annum, with H1 revenue of ₹22 crores versus ₹0.64 crores in the same period last year.

points.label: Phase 2 timeline
points.text: Partially operational by November end, fully operational by January, with management trying to prepone by one month; no additional customer approvals needed because the stud and bolt facility is already approved.

points.label: Ramp-up expected to be swift
points.text: Management sees no big gap or lag effect and expects to start using the new capacity within 15 days to 1 month, subject to order flow.

points.label: FY28 capacity bridge
points.text: Q1 and Q2 FY28 demand can be met with current Wada capacity plus Chennai Phase 2; Q3 may require temporary rented space; Q4 targets readiness of the new Wada facility.

points.label: Chennai utilization trajectory
points.text: From 35% in FY26 to a targeted 70% in FY27, with management noting that 70% may prove slightly conservative based on current order flow; FY28 utilization seen at 80%–90%.

points.label: Land search for FY29
points.text: Applied twice to SIPCOT for 3–5 acres near the existing plant but was unsuccessful; now exploring private channels, with a backup plan to shift the stud facility to long-lease premises and add bolt capacity in owned premises.

quotes.text: Balkishan Jalan: "I don't see there will be any big gap or lag effect. Subject to order flow we should be able to start using capacity in 15 days to 1 month time."

points.label: 10-acre land acquired near current Wada plant
points.text: MOU signed June 2026, legal details nearly finished, draft agreement shared with the seller.

points.label: Phased development to double capacity
points.text: The land will be developed in at least 2–3 phases, taking total capacity from ₹450 crores to ₹900 crores over time.

points.label: Near-term backup plan
points.text: Management is internally targeting partial operational readiness by FY28 Q4, creating ₹100 crores of capacity to take the total to ₹550 crores, serving as a backup in case of government approval delays.

points.label: FY28 capex unchanged
points.text: ₹40–45 crores planned, sufficient to support over ₹100 crores of incremental turnover; additional term loan may be raised next year depending on fund flow.

points.label: DSS and SFS fastener capacity
points.text: is planned for the new facility, with additions expected in FY28.

quotes.text: Balkishan Jalan: "This INR450 crores capacity will take to our INR550 crores so that we can meet the FY28 number with this capacity as a backup plan in case there is any further delay in any government approval or completing the capacity."

points.label: H1 EBITDA margin improved 1.3% net
points.text: Raw material cost rose due to product mix, but manpower cost reduced as a percentage and other expenses fell by 2.2%, primarily because the forex loss incurred in H1 FY26 did not repeat.

points.label: Employee cost trend favorable
points.text: In absolute terms, employee cost rose marginally (0.7% half-yearly) as headcount was added for market development in Europe and the US, but as a percentage of revenue it declined; management expects a lower percentage in H2.

points.label: Inventory remains elevated by design
points.text: Management attributes high inventory to the business model: 800+ SKUs, imports, 38% export share with goods in transit counted as inventory, and 24%–30% growth requiring forward inventory; working internally to reduce levels by a further 10%.

points.label: Receivables stretched by export shift
points.text: Trade receivables rose as export mix moved from 33% to 38%, with export working capital cycles running 90–100 days.

points.label: KPMG working capital study completed
points.text: Diagnostic analysis submitted; internal team to be formed and implementation to start early FY28, with benefits expected to accrue over 1 to 1.5 years.

points.label: Solar plant to add ~₹1.35 crores annually
points.text: The 1.2 MW open-access plant in Nanded, Maharashtra was commissioned October 30, 2026 at a capex of ₹6.2 crores; payback estimated at 4.5 years.

quotes.text: Balkishan Jalan: "KPMG has completed its diagnoses analysis and have submitted that report very recently. The company will work on its recommendations and we will be forming an internal team and start the implementation sometime early in FY28. But it will take at least 1 to 1.5 years for the benefits to accrue the company."

points.label: DSS and SFS are the growth engines
points.text: Both segments are developing domestic and global markets; CSS is mainly India-focused and therefore growing more slowly.

points.label: Disc springs growing 25%–30% from Wada
points.text: Management pushed back on an analyst's calculation that Wada growth ex-Chennai was only ~7%, pointing to disc spring performance; after providing Chennai numbers, the analyst recalculated Wada growth at ~10%, which management did not dispute.

points.label: Renewable energy and industrial to dominate mix
points.text: Over the next 2–3 years, management sees renewable energy at 35%–37%, industrial at 35%–37%, and mobility at 25% of revenue.

points.label: Disc springs and fasteners to reach 40%–42% of turnover
points.text: over 3–4 years, with DSS at 10%–12%.

points.label: Exotic materials capability already in place
points.text: Gala works with Inconel 177PH in DSS, supplying disc springs and precision stamp parts for turbocharger high-temperature applications, and Inconel coil springs for BS6 heavy commercial vehicles.

points.label: Aerospace deprioritized for now
points.text: Management sees a long gestation period for approvals and prefers to focus on opportunities where it is already seeing 25% YoY growth over the next 3–4 years; may reconsider in the near future.

quotes.text: Balkishan Jalan: "Aerospace basically need a long gestation period for approvals and all. So we thought before that there are other lot of opportunities are there. So why not to encourage that where we are already seeing 25% growth year-on-year in next 3, 4 years."

points.label: Electrolyzer: first bulk order dispatched
points.text: Received June 2026 from a leading manufacturer; ~₹2 crores sales expected in FY27; in advanced discussions for sample development with two other electrolyzer companies, one export and one global company manufacturing in India.

points.label: Electrolyzer, railway safety, and offshore wind combined
points.text: could deliver ₹40–50 crores revenue over the next 2–3 years, conditional on approvals and ramp-up.

points.label: European auto client progressing
points.text: At pilot lot supply stage for a European customer with manufacturing in India; multiple pilot lots to be supplied in Q3 and Q4 FY27; discussions started with other Tier 1 companies for similar applications, with inquiries and RFQs received this quarter.

points.label: Offshore wind exports began this quarter
points.text: Smart fasteners for offshore wind applications shipped, marking a move up the value chain.

points.label: Export growth seen as sustainable
points.text: for at least the next 3–4 years in Europe and the US, driven by new customer acquisition and local hires in both regions.

points.label: Competitive intensity stable
points.text: No major change in recent quarters; growth is coming from new customer additions rather than share gains within existing accounts.

quotes.text: Satish Kotwani: "Our base is still very small compared to the demand of these wind turbines companies, and our share of business with most of the wind companies is between 5% to 25%-30%. So there's enough room to grow with these wind companies."

items.title: Chennai fastener Phase 2 ramp
items.text: Phase 2 at the Vallam-Vadagal plant becomes operational by January 2027 (possibly preponed a month), adding ~₹50 crore of capacity to take Chennai to ~₹110 crore annually, with no fresh approvals needed since the stud and bolt facility is already OEM-audited. Management targets ₹9-10 crore/month by Q4 FY27 and 80-90% utilisation in FY28, turning the plant toward EBITDA parity with Wada by Q4 FY27 or Q1 FY28.

items.title: Wada 10-acre expansion
items.text: A ₹9 crore, 10-acre parcel adjacent to the Wada plant is under final agreement after the June 2026 MOU, with ₹58 crore of bank finance secured including a ₹28 crore term loan. A ₹40-45 crore building plan targets first capacity by Q4 FY28, lifting group capacity from ₹450 crore toward ₹550 crore and eventually supporting a doubling to ₹900 crore.

items.title: Wind fastener share gains
items.text: Gala supplies 5-30% of most wind customers' requirements and targets 15-20% share of India's wind turbine fastener market over two to three years, with price agreements signed with four leading wind OEMs for new Chennai bolts. Management targets 25-30% growth in the wind category in the short term, backed by a current order book it sees sustaining for at least 1-2 years.

items.title: Offshore wind fasteners
items.text: Critical fastener supplies to a European OEM began in Q4 FY26 and are ramping, with customer approvals received for offshore applications. Management guides offshore wind to ~10% of fastener sales by end-FY27, and these export customers carry better margins.

items.title: Electrolyzer order ramp
items.text: A first bulk commercial order from a leading Indian electrolyzer maker, received in June 2026, is already dispatching with ~₹2 crore of sales expected this financial year, and sample approvals are in advanced discussion with two more electrolyzer companies. Electrolyzers, offshore wind and railway safety together carry an estimated ₹40-50 crore revenue potential over the next 2-3 years.

items.title: Seatbelt retractor springs
items.text: A customer approved Gala in July 2026 after process audit and sample sign-off in India and Europe, replacing a German supplier with small-batch supplies starting before ramp. The customer is positive on raising Gala's share mid-to-long term, and Gala is approaching other buyers of the same German-made springs.

items.title: Europe export share gains
items.text: Exports rose to 38% of revenue in Q2 FY27, with 40% order booking growth in Europe driven by share taken from European manufacturers at a 10-20% cost advantage. The EU-India FTA expected in January 2027 would cut the current 3.7% import duty to zero.

items.title: Nanded solar savings
items.text: The 1.20 MW open-access solar plant at Nanded was commissioned on 30 October 2026 for ₹6.2 crore of capex. It should save about ₹1.3 crore a year in power costs at the Wada facilities, with payback in roughly four and a half years.
